key_insight: LLMs can translate mathematical statements across subfields, but they often change the level of generality rather than preserving the implicit hypothesis structure needed for faithful theory-to-theory translation.
engineering_relevance: For math-proof and scientific-text systems, evaluation must test whether models preserve scope and assumptions, not just whether outputs look plausible or pass external correctness filters.
method: Built a judge-free translation benchmark using separate queues for truth, content, and scope.
Measured whether rewrites recover the implicit hypothesis level in source statements.
Validated sensitivity with a planted-positive control and checked robustness on held-out and human-written items.
evidence_signal: Across seven models, translations toward more general framing widened quantification in 60.6% of rewrites, while translations toward concrete framing narrowed it in 28.3%; the pattern held on held-out and mathematician-written statements.
watch_item: The benchmark targets implicit-hypothesis preservation, so results may not directly generalize to broader natural-language or proof-generation settings without similar scope-aware evaluation.
paper_title: Objects Without Morphisms: What LLMs for Mathematics Do Not Represent
